'on':
  execute:
    inputs:
      resource_and_execution:
        label: Resource & Execution
        type: group
        collapsed: false
        items:
          resource:
            label: Resource Target
            type: compute-clusters
            autoselect: true
            optional: false
          scheduler:
            label: Submit as a Scheduler Job
            type: boolean
            default: false
            hidden: ${{ inputs.resource_and_execution.resource.schedulerType == '' }}
            tooltip: |
              On, the whole stack runs as one batch job on a compute node,
              submitted in the resource's scheduler dialect (Slurm or PBS),
              optionally with a vLLM model serve on the node's GPUs; the app
              ends with the walltime and relaunches reuse the corpus, index,
              and session names. Off, the app runs on the login node and
              outlives the workflow. Scheduler placement runs the container
              source only.
      slurm:
        label: Slurm Job
        type: group
        collapsed: false
        hidden: ${{ inputs.resource_and_execution.resource.schedulerType != 'slurm' || inputs.resource_and_execution.scheduler == false }}
        items:
          account:
            label: Account
            type: slurm-accounts
            resource: ${{ inputs.resource_and_execution.resource }}
            optional: true
            ignore: ${{ inputs.resource_and_execution.resource.schedulerType != 'slurm' || inputs.resource_and_execution.scheduler == false }}
            tooltip: Scheduler account for the job (--account).
          partition:
            label: Partition
            type: slurm-partitions
            resource: ${{ inputs.resource_and_execution.resource }}
            optional: true
            ignore: ${{ inputs.resource_and_execution.resource.schedulerType != 'slurm' || inputs.resource_and_execution.scheduler == false }}
            tooltip: Partition with the GPUs (--partition). Empty uses the cluster default.
          qos:
            label: Quality of Service
            type: slurm-qos
            resource: ${{ inputs.resource_and_execution.resource }}
            optional: true
            ignore: ${{ inputs.resource_and_execution.resource.schedulerType != 'slurm' || inputs.resource_and_execution.scheduler == false }}
            tooltip: QOS for the job (--qos), where the site requires one.
          walltime:
            label: Walltime
            type: string
            default: '02:00:00'
            tooltip: The stack ends with the job (--time). Relaunching reuses the corpus, index, and session names.
          scheduler_directives:
            label: Extra Scheduler Directives
            type: string
            default: ''
            optional: true
            tooltip: Semicolon-separated sbatch directives without the
      pbs:
        label: PBS Job
        type: group
        collapsed: false
        hidden: ${{ inputs.resource_and_execution.resource.schedulerType != 'pbs' || inputs.resource_and_execution.scheduler == false }}
        items:
          account:
            label: Account
            type: string
            default: ''
            optional: true
            tooltip: Allocation for the job (-A).
          queue:
            label: Queue
            type: string
            default: ''
            optional: true
            tooltip: Queue for the job (-q). Empty uses the cluster default.
          walltime:
            label: Walltime
            type: string
            default: '02:00:00'
            tooltip: The stack ends with the job (-l walltime=). Relaunching reuses the corpus, index, and session names.
          scheduler_directives:
            label: Extra Scheduler Directives
            type: string
            default: -l select=1:ngpus=1
            optional: true
            tooltip: Semicolon-separated qsub directives without the
      session_settings:
        label: Session
        type: group
        collapsed: false

            label: Session Name
            type: string
            default: studio

          unique_suffix:
            label: Append Port to Session Name
            type: boolean
            default: false

            optional: true
            tooltip: Banner background as
          suggested_prompts:

            type: string
            default: ''
            optional: true
            tooltip: Semicolon-separated example questions shown on the empty chat page. Empty keeps the app defaults; editable later in Settings.
          workdir:
            label: Work Directory

          source:

Pulled and cached once per host when soffice is absent, like the Node runtime, so Word, PowerPoint and Excel files render as pages. Leave empty to fall back to extracted-text previews.
          app_port:
            label: App Port
            type: number
            default: 0
            hidden: true
      kb_settings:

        type: group
        collapsed: false
        items:

            label: Knowledge Base Directory
            type: string
            default: ${HOME}/knowledge-base
            tooltip: The directory to index and serve. Created if missing; point it at an existing corpus to work over it.
          index_base:

            type: string
            default: ''
            optional: true

          starter_dirs:

            optional: true

            default: ''

Takes a bucket URI, a path on the resource, or several of either separated by semicolons, in which case the first that works is used. A knowledge base that already has content is never touched. Scheduler placement only.
          kb_label:
            label: Knowledge Base Label

jobs:
  setup:
    if: ${{ inputs.resource_and_execution.scheduler != true }}
    ssh:
      remoteHost: ${{ inputs.resource_and_execution.resource.ip }}
    steps:
      - name: Create directories
        run: |
          mkdir -p ${{ inputs.app_settings.workdir }}
          mkdir -p ${{ inputs.kb_settings.kb_root }}
          if [ -n "${{ inputs.kb_settings.index_base }}" ]; then
            mkdir -p "${{ inputs.kb_settings.index_base }}"
          fi
  get_ports:
    if: ${{ inputs.resource_and_execution.scheduler != true }}
    outputs:
      APP_PORT: ${{ needs.get_ports.steps.ports.outputs.APP_PORT }}
    ssh:
      remoteHost: ${{ inputs.resource_and_execution.resource.ip }}
    steps:
      - name: Get open port
        id: ports
        run: |
          if [[ ${{ inputs.app_settings.app_port }} == "0" ]]; then
            APP_PORT=$(pw agent open-port)
          else
            APP_PORT=${{ inputs.app_settings.app_port }}
          fi
          echo "App port: $APP_PORT"
          echo APP_PORT=$APP_PORT >> $OUTPUTS
  pull_software:
    if: ${{ inputs.resource_and_execution.scheduler != true }}
    needs:
      - setup
    ssh:
      remoteHost: ${{ inputs.resource_and_execution.resource.ip }}
    steps:
      - name: Put the app in place
        run: |
          if [ "${{ inputs.session_settings.session_method }}" = "cleanup" ]; then
            echo "Cleanup run; nothing to pull."
            exit 0
          fi
          if [ "${{ inputs.app_settings.source }}" = "container" ]; then
            CDIR="${{ inputs.app_settings.container_dir }}"
            [ -n "$CDIR" ] || CDIR="${{ inputs.app_settings.workdir }}"
            mkdir -p "$CDIR" || { echo "ERROR: cannot create $CDIR"; exit 1; }
            cd "$CDIR"
            IMG="${{ inputs.app_settings.image_path }}"
            [ -n "$IMG" ] || IMG="$PWD/studio.sif"
            command -v apptainer >/dev/null 2>&1 || command -v singularity >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
              { echo "ERROR: neither apptainer nor singularity is on the resource"; exit 1; }
            RUNTIME="$(command -v apptainer || command -v singularity)"
            case "$IMG" in
              pw://*|s3://*|gs://*|az://*)
                # Platform buckets are not something the container runtime
                # can pull; stage through the CLI instead.
                echo "Staging image from bucket: $IMG"
                # The CLI draws a carriage-return progress bar, which the
                # platform log viewer renders as one endless line; keep the
                # transcript readable and surface only the outcome.
                pw buckets cp "$IMG" "$PWD/studio.sif" > bucket-cp.log 2>&1 \
                  || { echo "ERROR: bucket copy failed"; tr '\r' '\n' < bucket-cp.log | tail -3; exit 1; }
                echo "staged image: $(du -h "$PWD/studio.sif" | cut -f1)"
                IMG="$PWD/studio.sif" ;;
              *://*)
                echo "Pulling image $IMG ..."
                "$RUNTIME" pull -F "$PWD/studio.sif" "$IMG" || { echo "ERROR: image pull failed"; exit 1; }
                IMG="$PWD/studio.sif" ;;
            esac
            [ -f "$IMG" ] || { echo "ERROR: container image not found: $IMG"; exit 1; }
            # A SIF is a squashfs image, and some login nodes run kernels
            # without squashfs (and without squashfuse or the privileges to
            # load the module). Where the runtime cannot mount the image,
            # expand it once into a sandbox directory and run from that;
            # unsquashfs needs no kernel support. Cached against the image's
            # timestamp so a rerun does not repeat the extraction.
            if "$RUNTIME" exec "$IMG" true 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "$IMG" > .image

              echo "Runtime cannot mount the image directly (no squashfs); expanding to a sandbox."
              command -v unsquashfs >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "ERROR: no squashfs support and unsquashfs is unavailable"; exit 1; }
              if [ -d sandbox ] && [ -f .sandbox-src ] && [ "$(cat .sandbox-src)" = "$IMG:$(stat -c %Y "$IMG")" ]; then

                FS_ID=$("$RUNTIME" sif list "$IMG" | awk -F'|' '$5 ~ /Squashfs/ { gsub(/ /, "", $1); print $1; exit }')

                rm -rf sandbox rootfs.squash
                "$RUNTIME" sif dump "$FS_ID" "$IMG" > rootfs.squash || { echo "ERROR: could not read the image partition"; exit 1; }
                # -no-xattrs: the destination is often a filesystem that
                # refuses them, and nothing in the image depends on them.
                unsquashfs -q -f -no-xattrs -d sandbox rootfs.squash || { echo "ERROR: sandbox expansion failed"; exit 1; }

          cd ${{ inputs.app_settings.workdir }}

          # from a GitHub release or the same file from a bucket. Each copy is
          # named by where it came from, so a relaunch on the same one keeps it.
          ASSET=activate-studio-linux-x86_64.tar.gz

            REF="${{ inputs.app_settings.git_ref }}"

            # is the current Stable release, the fixed "linux" release.

            else

                else

                fi
              }
            fi
            if ! tar -tzf incoming.tar.gz activate-studio/app/bin/studio-server >/dev/null 2>&1; then

              echo "A bundle made before the Go version carries the Node server; make one with deploy/make_bundle.sh."

            mkdir payload.new

            rm -f incoming.tar.gz

            rm -rf payload.new/bin payload.new/share payload.new/install.sh payload.new/uninstall.sh

            rm -rf payload.prev
            if [ -d payload ]; then mv payload payload.prev; fi
            mv payload.new payload
            echo "$KEY" > .bundle
          fi
          # The Node version's tree goes. With no index directory set, its
          # index, settings and credential store were app/index; they become
          # data/index.
          if [ -d app/index ] && [ -z "${{ inputs.kb_settings.index_base }}" ] && [ ! -e data/index ]; then

            echo "Moved the index, settings and credentials from app/index to data/index."
          fi
          rm -rf app node-runtime node-*-linux-x64.tar.xz gufi-install GUFI gufi-src.tar.gz cache repo
          echo "app: $(tr -d '\n ' < payload/app/build-info.json 2>/dev/null)"
      - name: Office rendering runtime when soffice is absent
        run: |
          cd ${{ inputs.app_settings.workdir }}
          RT_URI="${{ inputs.app_settings.office_runtime }}"
          if [ -z "$RT_URI" ]; then echo "No office runtime configured."; exit 0; fi
          if command -v soffice >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "System soffice present; staged runtime not needed."; exit 0; fi
          SOFFICE="$(find "$PWD/office-runtime" -name soffice -path "*/program/*" 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
          if [ -z "$SOFFICE" ]; then
            PW_BIN="$(command -v pw || echo pw)"
            "$PW_BIN" buckets cp "$RT_URI" office-runtime.tar.gz || { echo "office runtime pull failed; office rendering stays unavailable."; exit 0; }
            tar -xzf office-runtime.tar.gz && rm -f office-runtime.tar.gz
            SOFFICE="$(find "$PWD/office-runtime" -name soffice -path "*/program/*" | head -1)"
          fi
          [ -n "$SOFFICE" ] || { echo "no soffice in the runtime; office rendering stays unavailable."; exit 0; }
          printf '#!/bin/bash\nexec "%s" "$@"\n' "$SOFFICE" > soffice-wrapper.sh
          chmod +x soffice-wrapper.sh
          echo "Office rendering via staged runtime: $SOFFICE"
      - name: Search by meaning model
        run: |
          # The ONNX model ships in the app; the index refers to it at
          # INDEX_BASE/models/minilm-l6, a link, so a new app's model is the
          # one used.
          if [ "${{ inputs.session_settings.session_method }}" = "cleanup" ]; then exit 0; fi
          if [ "${{ inputs.app_settings.source }}" = "container" ]; then
            echo "Container mode; the image carries the model."
            exit 0
          fi
          cd ${{ inputs.app_settings.workdir }}
          INDEX_BASE="${{ inputs.kb_settings.index_base }}"
          [ -n "$INDEX_BASE" ] || INDEX_BASE="$PWD/data/index"
          mkdir -p "$INDEX_BASE/models"
          if [ -L "$INDEX_BASE/models/minilm-l6" ] || [ ! -e "$INDEX_BASE/models/minilm-l6" ]; then
            ln -sfn "$PWD/payload/models/minilm-l6" "$INDEX_BASE/models/minilm-l6"
          fi
          echo "Search by meaning model: $(ls "$INDEX_BASE/models/minilm-l6/" | tr '\n' ' ')"

          cd ${{ inputs.app_settings.workdir }}

          # The pid file is best effort; the sweep below catches watchdogs
          # whose pid file is stale or was written wrong.
          if [ -f watchdog.pid ]; then

          done
          if [ -f app-custom.pids ]; then
            echo "Stopping processes from a prior launch:"; cat app-custom.pids || true
            while read -r p; do
              [ -n "$p" ] || continue
              kill "$p" 2>/dev/null || true
              kill -- -"$p" 2>/dev/null || true

            ${REQUIRE_PERSONAL_KEY:+--env REQUIRE_PERSONAL_KEY="${REQUIRE_PERSONAL_KEY}"} \

            exit 0

            # resolves to nothing, and it hides from anyone reading the session
            # list that the deployment is down. The watchdog below restarts the
            # app and re-registers, which covers the case --keep was there for.
            setsid nohup "$PW_BIN" endpoints http -o text --name "$EP_NAME" --subdomain "$EP_NAME" "$PORT" > endpoint.log 2>&1 < /dev/null &

            # on the same port, so the endpoint keeps serving the same URL.
            # If the endpoint agent process dies, kill what is left of this
            # deployment (servers scoped by workdir, the agent by recorded
            # pid) and re-run this script for a clean start. Liveness uses the app health URL and
            # the agent pid file; matching the agent by command line proved
            # unreliable. A workflow relaunch kills the watchdog first, so
            # the two never fight.

          cd "\$(dirname "\$0")"
          while sleep 120; do
            app=1; agent=1
            curl -sf -m 8 "localhost:${PORT}/healthz" > /dev/null || app=0
            kill -0 "\$(cat agent.pid 2>/dev/null)" 2>/dev/null || agent=0
            [ "\$app\$agent" = 11 ] && continue
            for p in \$(pgrep -f "app/server/dist/main[.]js|payload/app/bin/studio-server" 2>/dev/null); do
              [ "\$(readlink /proc/\$p/cwd 2>/dev/null)" = "\$PWD" ] && kill "\$p" 2>/dev/null
            done
            sleep 3
            if [ "\$agent" = 1 ]; then
              echo "\$(date -Is) server unhealthy; restarting the server only" >> watchdog.log
              STUDIO_APP_ONLY=1 bash "${RUN_SCRIPT}" >> watchdog.log 2>&1
            else
              echo "\$(date -Is) endpoint agent gone; restarting stack" >> watchdog.log
              kill "\$(cat agent.pid 2>/dev/null)" 2>/dev/null
              bash "${RUN_SCRIPT}" >> watchdog.log 2>&1
            fi
            sleep 60

            exit 0
          fi

          # One stack per session name: end any previous job before submitting.
          cancel_by_name
          # A fresh output file per submission: a watcher reading a prior
          # job's leftover output mistakes its state for this run's.
          OUT="$RUNDIR/job-$(date +%s).out"
          ln -sf "$OUT" "$RUNDIR/job.out"
          # CLI-supplied partial input groups arrive with unset fields empty
          # (form defaults live only in the form), so walltime is backed by
          # a fallback; empty partition, account, qos, and queue mean the
          # flag is omitted and the cluster default applies.
          if [ "$STYPE" = "slurm" ]; then
            WALLTIME='${{ inputs.slurm.walltime }}'; [ -n "$WALLTIME" ] || WALLTIME='02:00:00'
            {
              echo "#SBATCH --job-name=$JOB_NAME"
              echo "#SBATCH --nodes=1"
              echo "#SBATCH --time=$WALLTIME"
              # Ask for SIGTERM at the batch shell a minute before the
              # walltime, so the cleanup trap has time to delete the
              # endpoint sessions instead of being killed outright and
              # leaving them behind as stopped records.
              echo "#SBATCH --signal=B:TERM@60"
              echo "#SBATCH --output=$OUT"
              [ -n "${{ inputs.slurm.partition }}" ] && echo "#SBATCH --partition=${{ inputs.slurm.partition }}"
              [ -n "${{ inputs.slurm.account }}" ] && echo "#SBATCH --account=${{ inputs.slurm.account }}"
              [ -n "${{ inputs.slurm.qos }}" ] && echo "#SBATCH --qos=${{ inputs.slurm.qos }}"
              DIRECTIVES='${{ inputs.slurm.scheduler_directives }}'
              IFS=';'
              for d in $DIRECTIVES; do d=$(echo "$d" | xargs); [ -n "$d" ] && echo "#SBATCH $d"; done
              unset IFS
              true
            } > headers.sh
          elif [ "$STYPE" = "pbs" ]; then
            WALLTIME='${{ inputs.pbs.walltime }}'; [ -n "$WALLTIME" ] || WALLTIME='02:00:00'
            {
              echo "#PBS -N $(echo "$JOB_NAME" | cut -c1-15)"
              echo "#PBS -o $OUT"
              echo "#PBS -j oe"
              echo "#PBS -l walltime=$WALLTIME"
              [ -n "${{ inputs.pbs.account }}" ] && echo "#PBS -A ${{ inputs.pbs.account }}"
              [ -n "${{ inputs.pbs.queue }}" ] && echo "#PBS -q ${{ inputs.pbs.queue }}"
              DIRECTIVES='${{ inputs.pbs.scheduler_directives }}'
              IFS=';'
              for d in $DIRECTIVES; do d=$(echo "$d" | xargs); [ -n "$d" ] && echo "#PBS $d"; done
              unset IFS
              true
            } > headers.sh
          else
            echo "ERROR: the resource reports no scheduler; turn off scheduler placement or pick a cluster with one."
            exit 1
          fi
          { head -1 job.sh; cat headers.sh; tail -n +2 job.sh; } > job-submit.sh
          chmod +x job-submit.sh
          sed -n '1,20p' job-submit.sh

          if [ "$STYPE" = "slurm" ]; then
            JOBID=$(sbatch job-submit.sh | grep -oE '[0-9]+$') || { echo "ERROR: submission failed"; exit 1; }
            job_state() { squeue -j "$JOBID" -h -o %T 2>/dev/null || true; }
            is_running() { [ "$1" = "RUNNING" ]; }
          else
            QSUB_OUT=$(qsub job-submit.sh 2>&1) || { echo "ERROR: submission failed: $QSUB_OUT"; exit 1; }
            JOBID=$(echo "$QSUB_OUT" | head -1)
            job_state() { qstat -f "$JOBID" 2>/dev/null | grep job_state | cut -d'=' -f2 | tr -d ' '; }
            is_running() { [ "$1" = "R" ]; }
          fi
          echo "Submitted job $JOBID"
          for i in $(seq 1 240); do
            ST=$(job_state)
            [ -z "$ST" ] && { echo "Job left the queue; output:"; tail -40 job.out 2>/dev/null; exit 1; }
            is_running "$ST" && break
            sleep 15
          done
          echo "Job running; waiting for the session URL..."
          URL=""
          for i in $(seq 1 240); do
            URL=$(grep -oE "https://[^ ]+" endpoint.log 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)
            [ -n "$URL" ] && { echo "Studio session: $URL"; break; }
            ST=$(job_state)
            [ -z "$ST" ] && { echo "Job ended before the session came up; output:"; tail -40 job.out 2>/dev/null; exit 1; }
            sleep 10
          done
          if [ "$METHOD" = "e2e" ]; then
            if [ -n "$URL" ]; then
              echo "E2E PASS: job ran, stack came up, session registered; cancelling the job."
              if [ "$STYPE" = "slurm" ]; then scancel "$JOBID"; else qdel "$JOBID"; fi
            else
              echo "E2E FAIL: session never came up; cancelling the job."
              if [ "$STYPE" = "slurm" ]; then scancel "$JOBID"; else qdel "$JOBID"; fi
              exit 1
            fi
            exit 0
          fi
          tail -5 job.out 2>/dev/null || true

scheduler.label: Submit as a Scheduler Job
scheduler.tooltip:
On, the whole stack runs as one batch job on a compute node,
submitted in the resource's scheduler dialect (Slurm or PBS),
optionally with a vLLM model serve on the node's GPUs; the app
ends with the walltime and relaunches reuse the corpus, index,
and session names. Off, the app runs on the login node and
outlives the workflow. Scheduler placement runs the container
source only.

partition.label: Partition
partition.tooltip: Partition with the GPUs (--partition). Empty uses the cluster default.

qos.label: Quality of Service
qos.tooltip: QOS for the job (--qos), where the site requires one.

walltime.label: Walltime
walltime.tooltip: The stack ends with the job (--time). Relaunching reuses the corpus, index, and session names.

queue.label: Queue
queue.tooltip: Queue for the job (-q). Empty uses the cluster default.

walltime.label: Walltime
walltime.tooltip: The stack ends with the job (-l walltime=). Relaunching reuses the corpus, index, and session names.

session_name.label: Session Name
session_name.tooltip: Session and endpoint name, and also the URL subdomain, so keep it stable across relaunches. Shell variables are expanded, so a name like studio-${USER} gives each person their own session and URL where several people launch the same workflow.

unique_suffix.label: Append Port to Session Name
unique_suffix.tooltip: Appends the app port to the session name so each launch gets a unique URL. Leave off for a stable URL that survives relaunches.

session_method.label: Session Method
session_method.tooltip:
Web     → pw endpoints http exposes the app at a root URL.
E2E     → launch everything, assert HTTP 200 at /healthz, tear down, exit.
Cleanup → stop every process prior launches left on the node, then exit.

app_name.label: App Name
app_name.tooltip: Product name shown in the interface (APP_NAME).

icon_path.label: Brand Icon Path
icon_path.tooltip: Image used as the interface brand icon and favicon (APP_ICON). Either an https URL, or an absolute path on the resource, in which case stage the file first (for a container deployment it must sit under a bind-mounted directory, such as a .branding folder inside the knowledge base).

icon_path_dark.label: Brand Icon Path (dark mode)
icon_path_dark.tooltip: Icon variant for dark mode; same rules as the light icon. Empty reuses the light icon.

banner_text.label: Classification Banner
banner_text.tooltip: Banner text across the top of the app, e.g. the CUI marking. The platform draws its own banner around an embedded session, so this one appears only when the app is opened on its own; editable later in Settings.

suggested_prompts.label: Chat Starter Prompts
suggested_prompts.tooltip: Semicolon-separated example questions shown on the empty chat page. Empty keeps the app defaults; editable later in Settings.

workdir.label: Work Directory
workdir.tooltip: Directory on the resource where the app is unpacked, built, and run.

source.label: App Source
source.tooltip:
Container → run a prebuilt Apptainer image of the Linux app
(deploy/app-go.def; each release publishes one to ghcr.io), so
host differences stop mattering.
GitHub release → download the Linux app of a release from GitHub
(needs outbound HTTPS to github.com); nothing is built on the
resource.
Bundle → the same Linux app (deploy/make_bundle.sh), pulled from the
bucket or pre-staged at <workdir>/bundle-prestage.tar.gz; nothing is
fetched from the internet.

options.label: Container (Apptainer image; pinned runtime, no build on the resource)
Bundle (bucket or pre-staged; for air-gapped systems)

container_dir.label: Container Scratch Directory
container_dir.tooltip: Where the image and its expanded sandbox live on the resource. Keep this on node-local disk, since it is derived from the image and costs nothing to recreate, while a shared filesystem charges for the space and extracts far more slowly.

image_path.label: Container Image
image_path.tooltip: Path to the .sif on the resource, a platform bucket URI (pw://user/bucket/studio.sif), or a library/docker URI the container runtime can pull. Several may be listed, separated by semicolons, and the first that works is used, so a shared copy can name a bucket behind it. Empty looks for studio.sif in the work directory.

repo_url.label: Repository URL
repo_url.tooltip: Repository whose releases carry the Linux app (activate-studio-linux-x86_64.tar.gz).

git_ref.label: Release
git_ref.tooltip: A release tag (such as v1.190), or main for the current Stable release.

bundlebucket.label: Bundle Bucket
bundlebucket.tooltip: Bucket holding the deployment bundle built by deploy/make_bundle.sh. If the platform bucket API is unavailable, pre-stage the bundle on the resource as <workdir>/bundle-prestage.tar.gz instead; the pull step falls back to it.

self_url.label: Public Studio URL
self_url.tooltip: The session URL this deployment is reached at (e.g. https://my-studio.example). Campaign agents running on other systems use it to reach the task board; empty keeps the board local-only.

bundle_file.label: Bundle File
bundle_file.tooltip: Filename of the bundle in the bucket. Bump to roll to a newer build.

refresh_software.label: Load Latest Bundle
refresh_software.tooltip: Replace the app in the work directory even when it came from the same release or bundle file; the index, settings and credentials are kept.

office_runtime.label: LibreOffice Runtime (bucket)
office_runtime.tooltip: Bucket path of an office-runtime.tar.gz (the official LibreOffice Linux binaries repacked as a relocatable directory). Pulled and cached once per host when soffice is absent, like the Node runtime, so Word, PowerPoint and Excel files render as pages. Leave empty to fall back to extracted-text previews.

kb_root.label: Knowledge Base Directory
kb_root.tooltip: The directory to index and serve. Created if missing; point it at an existing corpus to work over it.

index_base.label: Index Directory
index_base.tooltip: Where the search index, settings, and credential store live. Empty keeps them in <workdir>/data/index; set an absolute path (e.g. a /shared location) to survive work-directory rebuilds.

starter_dirs.label: Starter Directories
starter_dirs.tooltip: Comma-separated directory names for a knowledge base that is new or empty (e.g. papers,software,datasets). Empty uses the default set, and a knowledge base that already holds content is never touched.

starter_bundle.label: Starter Knowledge Base (bucket)
starter_bundle.tooltip: Tarball pulled and extracted into an empty knowledge base on first launch, so a fresh deployment starts with a working corpus. Takes a bucket URI, a path on the resource, or several of either separated by semicolons, in which case the first that works is used. A knowledge base that already has content is never touched. Scheduler placement only.

mission.label: Mission and Context
mission.tooltip: One short paragraph on what this Studio is for; injected into the assistant's system prompt and editable later in Settings.

libraries.label: Additional Libraries
libraries.tooltip:
Other indexes this Studio mounts read only, as a JSON list. Each entry
needs an id and an indexRoot (a GUFI tree); a label and a sourceRoot
(where the files are, when they are on this host) are optional.
Example: [{"id":"scratch","label":"Scratch","indexRoot":"/gufi/scratch"}]

sections.label: Visible Sections
sections.tooltip:
Comma-separated list of the sections to show, from chat, library,
search, query, overview, history, agents, workflows. Leave empty for all of them.
"library,search,overview" makes the Studio an index viewer with no assistant.

workflows.label: Offered Workflows
workflows.tooltip:
Comma-separated workflows to offer as tiles on the Workflows tab, in
order: account workflow names, marketplace/<slug>, or
github.com/<owner>/<repo>[/path][@ref]. Each viewer runs them under
their own account.
Administrators can also pick them in Settings, Workflows, from the
workflows on the account this Studio is deployed under.

build_gufi.label: Build GUFI Index Engine
build_gufi.tooltip: Kept for saved inputs. GUFI ships built in the app, so nothing is built on the resource.

run_index.label: Index on Launch
run_index.tooltip: Start a full index (metadata, text extraction, embeddings) once the server answers; the Studio serves while it builds. Turn off for a relaunch on an unchanged corpus, which the server keeps in sync as files change.

posture.label: Deployment Posture
posture.tooltip:
Single user runs with no platform identity and never creates the
per-user credential store. Multi-user postures verify the platform
identity header; shared keeps everyone on the deployment credential
with key collection hard-disabled, personal lets users add their own
model keys, strict requires them for chat. Multi-user postures need
the platform host below.

options.label: Single user (no identity, deployment credential only)

platform_host.label: Platform Host (multi-user postures)
platform_host.tooltip: Platform host for identity verification, e.g. activate.parallel.works; the JWKS path is appended automatically. Ignored for the single-user posture.

pw_api_key.label: Platform API key
pw_api_key.tooltip: A platform API key from your ACTIVATE account (Account, API keys), not an AI gateway or model key. The deployment's endpoint agent, CLI calls, and campaign runner authenticate with it, so the host never depends on a pw login that expires.

gateway_url.label: Gateway Base URL
gateway_url.tooltip: Override the OpenAI-compatible endpoint base URL (defaults to the ACTIVATE platform gateway).

serve.label: Serve a Model in the Job
serve.tooltip: Scheduler placement only. Start vLLM on the job's GPUs and point the Studio at it; off, the Studio uses the gateway settings above.

model_dir.label: Model Directory
model_dir.tooltip: HuggingFace-format model directory on the resource. Empty derives <workdir>/models/<model id>. Downloaded on the login node when missing and a model id is set; a read-only shared copy is served in place, so one copy covers every user.

hf_model_id.label: HuggingFace Model ID
hf_model_id.tooltip: Downloaded into the model directory when it does not exist yet.

vllm_image.label: vLLM Image (bucket or path)
vllm_image.tooltip: Bucket URI or path of the vLLM Apptainer image, or several separated by semicolons, the first that works being used. Staged beside the Studio image and cached on the resource.

gpu_ids.label: GPU IDs
gpu_ids.tooltip: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES for the model server. The Studio itself needs no GPU.

vllm_args.label: vLLM Arguments
vllm_args.tooltip: Tool-call and reasoning parsers are model-specific; a Gemma 4 model wants --tool-call-parser gemma4 --reasoning-parser gemma4 and its chat template, a Qwen model --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --reasoning-parser qwen3.

register_openai.label: Register the Model in the Catalog
register_openai.tooltip: Also expose the served model as a platform model (pw endpoints --openai), so other tools can use it while the job runs.

model_endpoint_name.label: Model Endpoint Name
model_endpoint_name.tooltip: Platform endpoint name for the served model, expanded like the session name, so gemma-${USER} gives each person their own. Empty derives <session name>-model.

out: Office rendering runtime when soffice is absent

Launch app on the login node
Stage directories, images, and starter corpus

permissions:
  - '*'
jobs:
  prepare:
    ssh:
      remoteHost: ${{ inputs.resource.ip }}
    steps:
      - name: Check inputs and write the index script
        run: |
          set -e
          # Each value goes through a quoted heredoc, so nothing in it is
          # expanded by this shell, and is quoted with %q when it is written
          # into the job script.
          cat > in.source_dir <<'STUDIO_GUFI_INPUT'
          ${{ inputs.index.source_dir }}
          STUDIO_GUFI_INPUT
          cat > in.index_dir <<'STUDIO_GUFI_INPUT'
          ${{ inputs.index.index_dir }}
          STUDIO_GUFI_INPUT
          cat > in.mode <<'STUDIO_GUFI_INPUT'
          ${{ inputs.index.mode }}
          STUDIO_GUFI_INPUT
          cat > in.threads <<'STUDIO_GUFI_INPUT'
          ${{ inputs.index.threads }}
          STUDIO_GUFI_INPUT
          cat > in.prefix <<'STUDIO_GUFI_INPUT'
          ${{ inputs.gufi.prefix }}
          STUDIO_GUFI_INPUT
          cat > in.source <<'STUDIO_GUFI_INPUT'
          ${{ inputs.gufi.source }}
          STUDIO_GUFI_INPUT
          value() { tr -d '\r' < "in.$1" | sed -e 's/^[[:space:]]*//' -e 's/[[:space:]]*$//' | sed -n '1p'; }
          fail() { echo "::error title=Invalid input::$1"; exit 1; }
          # ~, $HOME, and $WORKDIR at the start of a path are expanded from
          # this account's environment on the cluster; nothing else is.
          expand() {
            case "$1" in
              "~") printf '%s' "$HOME" ;;
              "~/"*) printf '%s/%s' "$HOME" "${1#\~/}" ;;
              '$HOME'|'${HOME}') printf '%s' "$HOME" ;;
              '$HOME/'*) printf '%s/%s' "$HOME" "${1#\$HOME/}" ;;
              '${HOME}/'*) printf '%s/%s' "$HOME" "${1#\$\{HOME\}/}" ;;
              '$WORKDIR'|'${WORKDIR}') printf '%s' "${WORKDIR:-}" ;;
              '$WORKDIR/'*) [ -n "${WORKDIR:-}" ] && printf '%s/%s' "$WORKDIR" "${1#\$WORKDIR/}" ;;
              '${WORKDIR}/'*) [ -n "${WORKDIR:-}" ] && printf '%s/%s' "$WORKDIR" "${1#\$\{WORKDIR\}/}" ;;
              *) printf '%s' "$1" ;;
            esac
          }

          # The default is the account's work directory on the cluster. Where
          # the cluster sets no $WORKDIR, the home directory is indexed.
          SOURCE_SPEC="$(value source_dir)"
          [ -n "$SOURCE_SPEC" ] || SOURCE_SPEC='$WORKDIR'
          case "$SOURCE_SPEC" in
            '$WORKDIR'|'${WORKDIR}')
              if [ -z "${WORKDIR:-}" ]; then
                echo "::warning title=No WORKDIR::\$WORKDIR is not set for $(whoami) on $(hostname -s); indexing the home directory instead."
                SOURCE_SPEC='$HOME'
              fi
              ;;
            '$WORKDIR/'*|'${WORKDIR}/'*)
              [ -n "${WORKDIR:-}" ] || fail "\$WORKDIR is not set for $(whoami) on $(hostname -s), so $SOURCE_SPEC cannot be resolved."
              ;;
          esac
          SOURCE_DIR="$(expand "$SOURCE_SPEC")"
          [ -n "$SOURCE_DIR" ] || fail "No directory to index was given."
          case "$SOURCE_DIR" in /*) ;; *) fail "The directory to index must be an absolute path or start with ~/ (got: $SOURCE_DIR)." ;; esac
          [ -d "$SOURCE_DIR" ] || fail "$SOURCE_DIR is not a directory on $(hostname -s)."
          [ -r "$SOURCE_DIR" ] && [ -x "$SOURCE_DIR" ] || fail "$SOURCE_DIR is not readable by $(whoami)."
          SOURCE_DIR="$(cd "$SOURCE_DIR" && pwd -P)"
          [ "$SOURCE_DIR" != "/" ] || fail "Indexing / is not supported; choose a directory."

          INDEX_DIR="$(expand "$(value index_dir)")"
          DEFAULT_INDEX_DIR=no
          if [ -z "$INDEX_DIR" ]; then
            DEFAULT_INDEX_DIR=yes
            name="$(printf '%s' "${SOURCE_DIR##*/}" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '_')"
            hash="$(printf '%s' "$SOURCE_DIR" | sha256sum | cut -c1-8)"
            INDEX_DIR="$HOME/.activate-studio/indexes/${name}-${hash}"
          fi
          case "$INDEX_DIR" in /*) ;; *) fail "The index directory must be an absolute path or start with ~/ (got: $INDEX_DIR)." ;; esac
          INDEX_DIR="$(realpath -m "$INDEX_DIR")"
          # An index inside the tree it indexes would index itself, and every
          # update would grow it; one that holds the tree would be swapped
          # over it. The one exception is the default location when the home
          # directory is indexed: the build then skips directories named
          # .activate-studio, and since an update cannot skip anything, it
          # always rebuilds.
          SKIP_NAME=""
          case "$INDEX_DIR/" in
            "$SOURCE_DIR/"*)
              if [ "$DEFAULT_INDEX_DIR" = yes ] && [ "$SOURCE_DIR" = "$(cd "$HOME" && pwd -P)" ]; then
                SKIP_NAME=.activate-studio
              else
                fail "The index directory $INDEX_DIR is inside $SOURCE_DIR. Choose an index directory outside the directory being indexed."
              fi
              ;;
          esac
          case "$SOURCE_DIR/" in "$INDEX_DIR/"*) fail "$SOURCE_DIR is inside the index directory $INDEX_DIR." ;; esac
          # Only a directory this workflow wrote, or an empty one, is used:
          # a rebuild replaces what is there.
          if [ -d "$INDEX_DIR" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$INDEX_DIR" 2>/dev/null)" ] && [ ! -f "$INDEX_DIR/.studio-index.json" ]; then
            fail "$INDEX_DIR already holds files this workflow did not write. Choose an empty or new index directory."
          fi

          MODE="$(value mode)"
          case "$MODE" in build|update) ;; "") MODE=update ;; *) fail "Mode must be build or update (got: $MODE)." ;; esac
          THREADS="$(value threads)"
          case "$THREADS" in ''|*[!0-9]*) THREADS=4 ;; esac
          [ "$THREADS" -ge 1 ] && [ "$THREADS" -le 256 ] || THREADS=4
          if [ -n "$SKIP_NAME" ] && [ "$MODE" = update ]; then
            echo "The index is inside the directory being indexed, so it is rebuilt rather than updated."
            MODE=build
          fi

          PREFIX="$(expand "$(value prefix)")"
          [ -n "$PREFIX" ] || PREFIX="$HOME/.activate-studio/gufi"
          case "$PREFIX" in /*) ;; *) fail "The GUFI prefix must be an absolute path or start with ~/ (got: $PREFIX)." ;; esac
          PREFIX="$(realpath -m "$PREFIX")"

          # The GUFI source: a git URL with @<ref>, or a pw:// tarball of a
          # GUFI source tree for systems that cannot reach GitHub. The install
          # is keyed by commit, or by a hash of the tarball's path.
          GUFI_SOURCE="$(value source)"
          [ -n "$GUFI_SOURCE" ] || GUFI_SOURCE="https://github.com/mar-file-system/GUFI@021a717a6089b9e28b068695dc7c7f3732fd1a56"
          case "$GUFI_SOURCE" in
            pw://*)
              GUFI_ID="tar-$(printf '%s' "$GUFI_SOURCE" | sha256sum | cut -c1-12)"
              ;;
            *@*)
              repo="${GUFI_SOURCE%@*}"; ref="${GUFI_SOURCE##*@}"
              if printf '%s' "$ref" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{40}$'; then
                GUFI_ID="$ref"
              else
                GUFI_ID="$(git ls-remote "$repo" "$ref" "refs/tags/$ref^{}" 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR==1 {print $1}')"
                [ -n "$GUFI_ID" ] || fail "Could not resolve $ref in $repo from $(hostname -s)."
              fi
              ;;
            *) fail "The GUFI source must be <git URL>@<commit, tag, or branch> or a pw:// tarball (got: $GUFI_SOURCE)." ;;
          esac
          GUFI_DIR="$PREFIX/$GUFI_ID"

          # The job script. Its exit status is recorded in a file because the
          # submitter does not report it; record checks it.
          SCRIPT="$PWD/gufi-index.sh"
          EXIT_FILE="$PWD/gufi-index.exit"
          rm -f "$EXIT_FILE"
          {
            echo '#!/bin/bash'
            printf 'EXIT_FILE=%q\n' "$EXIT_FILE"
            printf 'GUFI_BIN=%q\n' "$GUFI_DIR/bin"
            printf 'GUFI_ID=%q\n' "$GUFI_ID"
            printf 'SOURCE_DIR=%q\n' "$SOURCE_DIR"
            printf 'INDEX_DIR=%q\n' "$INDEX_DIR"
            printf 'MODE=%q\n' "$MODE"
            printf 'THREADS=%q\n' "$THREADS"
            printf 'SKIP_NAME=%q\n' "$SKIP_NAME"
          } > "$SCRIPT"
          cat >> "$SCRIPT" <<'STUDIO_GUFI_SCRIPT'
          set -euo pipefail
          trap 'echo $? > "$EXIT_FILE"' EXIT
          export PATH="$GUFI_BIN:$PATH"
          json() { printf '"%s"' "$(printf '%s' "$1" | sed -e 's/\\/\\\\/g' -e 's/"/\\"/g')"; }

          base="$(basename "$SOURCE_DIR")"
          tree="$INDEX_DIR/$base"
          manifest="$INDEX_DIR/.studio-index.json"
          mkdir -p "$INDEX_DIR"
          started="$(date +%s)"
          previous="$( { sed -n 's/.*"startedAt": *\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null || true; } | head -1)"
          echo "Indexing $SOURCE_DIR into $tree on $(hostname -s) with $THREADS threads (mode $MODE)"

          # gufi_incremental_update resolves the tree's entries relative to its
          # working directory and creates (and removes) a temporary database
          # there, so it runs from the directory that holds the tree, which
          # must be writable. Where it is not, as for a work directory under
          # a site-owned parent, the index is rebuilt instead.
          parent="$(dirname "$SOURCE_DIR")"
          can_update=no
          if [ "$MODE" = update ] && [ -f "$tree/db.db" ] && [ -n "$previous" ]; then
            if [ -w "$parent" ]; then
              can_update=yes
            else
              echo "An update writes a temporary file in $parent, which $(whoami) cannot write; rebuilding instead."
            fi
          fi

          if [ "$can_update" = yes ]; then
            # Only directories changed since the previous run are rescanned,
            # with a minute's margin for clock skew between nodes.
            action=update
            park="$INDEX_DIR/.parking"
            rm -rf "$park"; mkdir -p "$park"
            cd "$parent"
            # The update names every directory it changes, so its output
            # goes to a log beside the index rather than into the run log.
            if ! gufi_incremental_update -n "$THREADS" --suspect-stat --suspect-method 3 \
              --suspect-time "$((previous - 60))" "$tree" "$SOURCE_DIR" "$park" > "$INDEX_DIR/.update.log" 2>&1; then
              echo "gufi_incremental_update failed; its output is in $INDEX_DIR/.update.log"
              exit 1
            fi
            cd "$INDEX_DIR"
            rm -rf "$park"
          else
            # A full build goes beside the current index and replaces it only
            # when complete.
            action=build
            rm -f "$INDEX_DIR/.update.log"
            stage="$INDEX_DIR/.build-$$"
            rm -rf "$stage"
            skip=()
            if [ -n "$SKIP_NAME" ]; then
              printf '%s\n' "$SKIP_NAME" > "$INDEX_DIR/.skip"
              skip=(--skip-file "$INDEX_DIR/.skip")
            fi
            gufi_dir2index -n "$THREADS" ${skip[@]+"${skip[@]}"} "$SOURCE_DIR" "$stage"
            [ -d "$stage/$base" ] || { echo "gufi_dir2index wrote no tree at $stage/$base"; exit 1; }
            if [ -d "$tree" ]; then mv "$tree" "$INDEX_DIR/.old-$$"; fi
            mv "$stage/$base" "$tree"
            rm -rf "$stage" "$INDEX_DIR/.old-$$"
          fi

          directories="$(gufi_query -n "$THREADS" -d ' ' -S "SELECT 1 FROM summary WHERE isroot = 1" "$tree" | wc -l)"
          entries="$(gufi_query -n "$THREADS" -d ' ' -E "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pentries" "$tree" | awk '{ s += $1 } END { print s + 0 }')"
          finished="$(date +%s)"
          {
            echo '{'
            echo '  "version": 1,'
            echo "  \"source\": $(json "$SOURCE_DIR"),"
            echo "  \"index\": $(json "$tree"),"
            echo "  \"indexDir\": $(json "$INDEX_DIR"),"
            echo "  \"mode\": $(json "$MODE"),"
            echo "  \"action\": $(json "$action"),"
            echo "  \"startedAt\": $started,"
            echo "  \"builtAt\": $(json "$(date -u -d "@$finished" +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"),"
            echo "  \"seconds\": $((finished - started)),"
            echo "  \"gufiCommit\": $(json "$GUFI_ID"),"
            echo "  \"gufiBin\": $(json "$GUFI_BIN"),"
            echo "  \"host\": $(json "$(hostname -s)"),"
            echo "  \"user\": $(json "$(whoami)"),"
            echo "  \"directories\": $directories,"
            echo "  \"files\": $entries"
            echo '}'
          } > "$manifest.tmp"
          mv "$manifest.tmp" "$manifest"
          echo "Index $action finished in $((finished - started))s: $directories directories, $entries files"
          STUDIO_GUFI_SCRIPT
          chmod 700 "$SCRIPT"

          echo "Directory:  $SOURCE_DIR"
          echo "Index:      $INDEX_DIR"
          echo "Mode:       $MODE, $THREADS threads"
          echo "GUFI:       $GUFI_SOURCE -> $GUFI_DIR"
          # Later jobs read these values from files rather than from
          # outputs, which are pasted into their scripts unquoted.
          printf '%s\n' "$GUFI_SOURCE" > state.gufi_source
          printf '%s\n' "$GUFI_ID" > state.gufi_id
          printf '%s\n' "$GUFI_DIR" > state.gufi_dir
          printf '%s\n' "$INDEX_DIR" > state.index_dir
          echo "STATE=$PWD/state" | tee -a $OUTPUTS
          echo "SCRIPT_PATH=$SCRIPT" | tee -a $OUTPUTS
          echo "EXIT_FILE=$EXIT_FILE" | tee -a $OUTPUTS
  install_gufi:
    needs:
      - prepare
    ssh:
      remoteHost: ${{ inputs.resource.ip }}
    steps:
      - name: Install GUFI if this commit is not installed
        run: |
          set -e
          STATE="${{ needs.prepare.outputs.STATE }}"
          GUFI_DIR="$(cat "$STATE.gufi_dir")"
          GUFI_ID="$(cat "$STATE.gufi_id")"
          GUFI_SOURCE="$(cat "$STATE.gufi_source")"
          if [ -f "$GUFI_DIR/.installed" ] && [ -x "$GUFI_DIR/bin/gufi_dir2index" ]; then
            echo "GUFI $GUFI_ID is installed at $GUFI_DIR."
            exit 0
          fi
          if ! command -v cmake >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v gcc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            module load cmake gcc >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          fi
          for tool in cmake gcc g++ make; do
            command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "::error title=Missing build tool::$tool is not on PATH on $(hostname -s); GUFI cannot be built here. Install it or load its module, or install GUFI at $GUFI_DIR by hand."; exit 1; }
          done

          # One install per commit at a time. mkdir is atomic on shared file
          # systems where flock may not be; a lock older than two hours is
          # taken to be left by a run that died.
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$GUFI_DIR")"
          lock="$GUFI_DIR.lock"
          locked=no
          for i in $(seq 1 240); do
            if mkdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null; then locked=yes; break; fi
            if [ -n "$(find "$lock" -maxdepth 0 -mmin +120 2>/dev/null)" ]; then rmdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null || true; continue; fi
            [ -f "$GUFI_DIR/.installed" ] && { echo "Another run installed GUFI $GUFI_ID."; exit 0; }
            sleep 15
          done
          [ "$locked" = yes ] || { echo "::error title=Install lock::Timed out waiting for $lock"; exit 1; }
          trap 'rmdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
          [ -f "$GUFI_DIR/.installed" ] && { echo "Another run installed GUFI $GUFI_ID."; exit 0; }

          build="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gufi-build.XXXXXX")"
          trap 'rmdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null || true; rm -rf "$build"' EXIT
          case "$GUFI_SOURCE" in
            pw://*)
              pw buckets cp "$GUFI_SOURCE" "$build/gufi-src.tar.gz" > "$build/cp.log" 2>&1 || { tr '\r' '\n' < "$build/cp.log" | tail -3; echo "::error title=GUFI source::Could not copy $GUFI_SOURCE"; exit 1; }
              mkdir -p "$build/src"
              tar -xzf "$build/gufi-src.tar.gz" -C "$build/src" --strip-components=1
              ;;
            *)
              # A blobless clone fetches file contents for the one commit only;
              # the tags stay, which GUFI's version string is built from.
              git clone --quiet --filter=blob:none --no-checkout "${GUFI_SOURCE%@*}" "$build/src"
              git -C "$build/src" -c advice.detachedHead=false checkout --quiet "$GUFI_ID"
              ;;
          esac
          [ -f "$build/src/CMakeLists.txt" ] || { echo "::error title=GUFI source::No CMakeLists.txt in the GUFI source"; exit 1; }
          # open() with O_CREAT needs a mode; compilers that enforce
          # _FORTIFY_SOURCE reject the call without one.
          sed -i 's/open(extdb_path, O_CREAT | O_WRONLY);/open(extdb_path, O_CREAT | O_WRONLY, S_IRUSR | S_IWUSR | S_IRGRP | S_IWGRP | S_IROTH);/' \
            "$build/src/src/gufi_query/spread_tree.c" 2>/dev/null || true

          # The system compilers, not whatever CC a site's default modules set,
          # so the binaries need no module loaded to run.
          export CC="$(command -v gcc)" CXX="$(command -v g++)"
          # GUFI's configure requires Python 3.9 or later; some systems'
          # python3 is older while a newer python3.X is installed beside it.
          python=""
          for p in python3 python3.13 python3.12 python3.11 python3.10 python3.9; do
            p="$(command -v "$p" 2>/dev/null)" || continue
            "$p" -c 'import sys; sys.exit(0 if sys.version_info >= (3, 9) else 1)' 2>/dev/null && { python="$p"; break; }
          done
          [ -n "$python" ] || { echo "::error title=Missing build tool::GUFI needs Python 3.9 or later on $(hostname -s); none was found."; exit 1; }
          # setfattr and getfattr are required at configure time but only
          # GUFI's tests run them; where they are missing, a command that
          # fails stands in, so anything that does call them fails visibly.
          xattr_args=""
          command -v setfattr >/dev/null 2>&1 || xattr_args="$xattr_args -DSETFATTR=/bin/false"
          command -v getfattr >/dev/null 2>&1 || xattr_args="$xattr_args -DGETFATTR=/bin/false"

          jobs="$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 4)"; [ "$jobs" -le 8 ] || jobs=8
          echo "Building GUFI $GUFI_ID into $GUFI_DIR with $jobs jobs on $(hostname -s) ($CC, $python)"
          # DEP_INSTALL_PREFIX inside the install prefix keeps the install
          # self-contained: the binaries' runtime paths point at it. Config
          # and completion default to /etc, which needs root.
          cmake -S "$build/src" -B "$build/b" $xattr_args \
            -DPython3_EXECUTABLE="$python" \
            -DPython3_SHEBANG="$python" \
            -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
            -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="$GUFI_DIR" \
            -DDEP_INSTALL_PREFIX="$GUFI_DIR/deps" \
            -DDEP_BUILD_THREADS="$jobs" \
            -DDEP_AI=Off \
            -DENABLE_SUDO_TESTS=Off \
            -DSERVER_CONFIG="$GUFI_DIR/etc/GUFI/config" \
            -DCLIENT_CONFIG="$GUFI_DIR/etc/GUFI/config" \
            -DBASH_COMPLETION=Off > "$build/configure.log" 2>&1 \
            || { tail -30 "$build/configure.log"; echo "::error title=GUFI build::cmake configure failed"; exit 1; }
          cmake --build "$build/b" -j "$jobs" > "$build/build.log" 2>&1 \
            || { tail -40 "$build/build.log"; echo "::error title=GUFI build::compile failed"; exit 1; }
          cmake --install "$build/b" > "$build/install.log" 2>&1 \
            || { tail -20 "$build/install.log"; echo "::error title=GUFI build::install failed"; exit 1; }
          "$GUFI_DIR/bin/gufi_dir2index" -v
          touch "$GUFI_DIR/.installed"
          echo "GUFI $GUFI_ID installed at $GUFI_DIR"
  index:
    needs:
      - prepare
      - install_gufi
    ssh:
      remoteHost: ${{ inputs.resource.ip }}
    steps:
      - name: Run the index script
        uses: marketplace/script_submitter/v3.6
        with:
          resource: ${{ inputs.resource }}
          shebang: '#!/bin/bash'
          use_existing_script: true
          script_path: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.SCRIPT_PATH }}
          define_cleanup_script: false
          scheduler: ${{ inputs.cluster.scheduler }}
          use_scheduler_agent: false
          submit_and_exit: false
          slurm:
            is_enabled: ${{ inputs.cluster.slurm.is_enabled }}
            account: ${{ inputs.cluster.slurm.account }}
            partition: ${{ inputs.cluster.slurm.partition }}
            qos: ${{ inputs.cluster.slurm.qos }}
            cpus_per_task: ${{ inputs.index.threads }}
            nodes: 1
            node_type: ''
            time: ${{ inputs.cluster.slurm.time }}
            scheduler_directives: ${{ inputs.cluster.slurm.scheduler_directives }}
          pbs:
            is_enabled: ${{ inputs.cluster.pbs.is_enabled }}
            account: ${{ inputs.cluster.pbs.account }}
            scheduler_directives: ${{ inputs.cluster.pbs.scheduler_directives }}
  record:
    needs:
      - prepare
      - index
    ssh:
      remoteHost: ${{ inputs.resource.ip }}
    steps:
      - name: Check the result and print the manifest
        run: |
          exit_file="${{ needs.prepare.outputs.EXIT_FILE }}"
          manifest="$(cat "${{ needs.prepare.outputs.STATE }}.index_dir")/.studio-index.json"
          if [ ! -f "$exit_file" ]; then
            echo "::error title=Index::No exit status in $exit_file; the index script did not run to its end"
            exit 1
          fi
          status="$(cat "$exit_file")"
          if [ "$status" != "0" ]; then
            echo "::error title=Index::The index script exited with status $status"
            exit 1
          fi
          # The Studio reads the manifest from between these markers in the
          # run log.
          echo "STUDIO_INDEX_BEGIN"
          cat "$manifest"
          echo "STUDIO_INDEX_END"
